sm: The host says Robert Pattinson has been cast as the new James Bond, and he sets out to rank the Bond actors from worst to best. He says Bond endures as male wish fulfillment, a handsome contract killer working for a righteous cause. He is optimistic about Pattinson because the film has a strong director in Denis Villeneuve and a strong writer in Steven Knight. Number six is George Lazenby, who starred in only one film, On Her Majesty's Secret Service, which the host calls the weakest of the franchise. He says Lazenby was found by a member of the Broccoli family and could not act, and he declined to return. Number five is Roger Moore, whom the host dislikes for playing Bond as a goofy, jokey caricature, though he grants that this may fit the novels. Number four is Timothy Dalton, who took Bond in a darker, more serious direction in The Living Daylights and License to Kill, but whose films the host says are not among the best.

Number three is Pierce Brosnan, the Bond the host grew up with. He calls him debonair and charming with a darker side, and praises his recent role as an unhinged mob leader. He also has a fondness for GoldenEye and its video game. Number two is Daniel Craig, whom the host admits to being a fan of. He likes the gritty physicality and calls Casino Royale the best Bond film by far. He rates Quantum of Solace and Spectre as weak, Skyfall as excellent, and No Time to Die as a disappointment, though he owns the Omega watch from that film. Number one is Sean Connery, who made Bond a cultural icon, with a light touch and a sense he could kill someone. The host calls him underrated and names The Hunt for Red October and The Man Who Would Be King as strong roles. He says Connery's films are not as good as Craig's but he will always be Bond to most people. He guesses Pattinson will land in the top three given the talent around him.
